title: pm-stack(aggregator): Meta keeper re-arm is all-or-nothing — a partial .backup rename is never restored and the alert falsely says no backups exist

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Summary

`pm-stack(aggregator)` Meta session keeper: the exporter re-arm check requires **both** systemd units (or **both** `.backup` copies) to be present, so a partial rename state — exactly the failure family the keeper was built to recover from (the 2026-11-01 → 11-05 incident, units renamed to `.backup`) — can never be recovered, and the alert then falsely states that no `.backup` copies exist.

## Evidence

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/meta-renewal.ts`, `defaultEnsureExporterArmed` (lines 102–125):

- Line 111: returns `"armed"` only if the timer **and** the service both exist.
- Line 114: restores only if the timer backup **and** the service backup both exist.
- Any mixed state (one unit present + the other unit's `.backup` present, or one unit missing with no backup while the other has one) falls through to `"missing"` (line ~123).
- The `exporter-missing` alert (lines 232–233) then says: "…are missing from ~/.config/systemd/user and **no .backup copies exist**" — which is false in the mixed state, and sends the human responder looking for units to recreate instead of a one-rename restore.

Verified this run on the laptop at `1dae17e457` with the real module (probe `~/git/fleet/probe-meta-partial/probe.ts`, fake `$HOME`, `readLatest` → null, `runExporter` injected; `ensureExporterArmed` **not** injected, so the default implementation ran):

| Fake `~/.config/systemd/user` contents | Result |
|---|---|
| `meta-quota-export.timer` + `meta-quota-export.service.backup` | `attention`, recovery `exporter-missing`, alert claims "no .backup copies exist"; the service backup was **not** restored |
| `meta-quota-export.service` + `meta-quota-export.timer.backup` | Same: `exporter-missing`, false alert, timer backup not restored |
| both `.backup` files, neither unit present (control) | Both units restored, exporter run attempted (`still-expired` against the null probe) — the all-or-nothing path works |
| empty dir (control) | `exporter-missing` — correct here |

The existing suite (`src/meta-renewal.test.ts`, 6 tests) injects `ensureExporterArmed` in every case, so the default implementation's filesystem logic has no test coverage at all.

## Why it matters

The keeper exists so the Nov-1 sequence (units renamed away → exporter silent → ~40h of unalerted stale quota data) cannot repeat silently. A partial rename — an interrupted restore, one unit renamed back by hand, one unit deleted while its backup remains — is a plausible variant of that same incident, and in that state the keeper (a) never recovers on its own even though everything needed is on disk, and (b) actively misdiagnoses the state in the one alert a human will read.

## Acceptance criteria

- `defaultEnsureExporterArmed` restores each missing unit independently from its own `.backup` copy when that copy exists (per-unit, not all-or-nothing), and reports `restored` when it restored at least one unit.
- The `exporter-missing` alert is only used when no unit and no `.backup` copy can be found; when a `.backup` copy exists but could not be restored (or only some units are present), the alert/state names the actual per-unit state.
- New tests exercise the **default** implementation against a fake unit directory (temp `$HOME` or an injectable unit dir): partial-backup states for each unit, both-backups, neither, and already-armed.
- Existing `meta-renewal.test.ts` tests still pass (`bun test src/meta-renewal.test.ts`).

Related: the keeper landed for #6079 (PR #6315); standing-rule follow-through is #6120 (this is a code defect in the keeper, not a missing keeper).
